title: The true bargain
told: a sakhi, a traditional story of Guru Nanak

hook.say: before the story, can i ask you something? if someone handed you some money and said “spend it well,” what would you do?
options: careful with it. i like that. listen to what one boy did.
then you might like this boy. listen.
honest. listen to what one boy did with his.

steps.line: When Guru Nanak was young, his father gave him twenty rupees and sent him to market. Make a good deal, he said. A true bargain.
steps.label: a traditional story

steps.line: On the road, Nanak met a group of holy men who had gone without food for days.

steps.q: Nanak has twenty rupees and a job to do. What do you think he does?
o: Spends it all on food for them
Gives them one rupee and goes on
Takes them home to his father
steps.why: He spent every rupee feeding them.

steps.line: He spent every rupee on flour, lentils and ghee, and fed them all.
He came home with empty hands. His father was furious. Where’s the deal?
Nanak said feeding the hungry is the truest deal there is. Sikhs remember the place as Sacha Sauda.

steps.q: Sacha Sauda is a real place today. What stands there?
steps.why: Gurdwara Sacha Sauda stands at Farooqabad, in Pakistan’s Punjab. Nanak’s birthplace, Nankana Sahib, is in Pakistan too.

steps.q: Decades later, an emperor comes to meet the third Guru. Where is he asked to sit first?
o: On a raised seat by the Guru
On the floor, in the row
In a tent of his own
steps.why: On the floor, with everyone, to eat the same meal.

steps.line: Sikh tradition says that when the emperor Akbar came to see the third Guru, he first sat on the floor and ate in the row with everyone.
steps.label: a traditional story

steps.q: The langar grew under the second Guru. Who ran its kitchen, and is praised for it in the Guru Granth Sahib?
steps.why: Mata Khivi ran the kitchen at Khadur Sahib. The Guru Granth Sahib praises her rice pudding with ghee, and her shade, like a leafy tree.

steps.line: Today gurdwaras everywhere keep a langar, a free kitchen. Simple vegetarian food, everyone in one row on the floor, the pangat. Any faith, or none.
steps.label: today

steps.q: Langar food is free. So who pays for it?
o: A small fee from each family
Daswandh: a tenth, given by Sikhs
steps.why: Many Sikhs set aside daswandh, a tenth of what they earn, and others give food or hours in the kitchen. No one is charged for the meal.

say: here’s what i love. his father asked for a good deal, and nanak found the best one: hungry people, fed.
sikhs carry that into every langar. the food is free, the floor is shared, and nobody sits higher.

steps.q: Langar food is simple and vegetarian. From what you’ve seen, why might that be?
o: So no guest has to ask what’s in it
Because meat cost too much then
So the cooks can work faster
steps.why: So nobody has to ask what’s in it. Any guest can sit down and eat.

today.say: any gurdwara’s langar is open to you, no questions asked. this week, find your nearest one, or share one simple meal with someone you’d never usually sit beside.
options: shoes off, head covered, sit in the row, hold out your hands. you’ll be fed.
that’s the true bargain, right there.

card.keepWhy: Twenty rupees, spent on strangers. The truest bargain.
